pr_title: make our testsuite pass in a podman container with default privs
pr_body:
Our tests so far mostly did a geteuid() == 0 check to guard privileged operations. Podman apparently invokes containers by default with geteuid() == 0 but then takes most caps away, which then means we'll try the privleged operaitons and fail. Let's tweak the conditioning hence.

Fixes: #19746
pr_comments: Force pushed a new version changing that one check to geteuid(). For the other thing see comment above. Uprgading green label

issue_context.title: test-suite failures inside Docker / Podman
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**

248.3

**Used distribution**

Debian sid

Triggered by #19733 I ran the systemd test suite inside Docker and also Podman.
If you want to reproduce the issue, install podman, then run the following command:
```
sudo podman run --name debian-sid -e LANG=C.UTF-8 -it debian:sid /bin/bash -x -c 'echo "deb-src http://ftp.debian.org/debian/ experimental main" >> /etc/apt/sources.list; apt update && apt upgrade -y && apt build-dep -y systemd; apt install -y systemd; systemd-detect-virt; systemd-detect-virt --container; apt-get source -b systemd'
```

```
Error: sd-bus call: Permission denied: OCI permission denied
```
Looking at the logs, it seems they are all connected to some issues in privileges/capabilities
Ah, possible. I used sudo. Lemme update the command line

So the test suite apparently fails if the cap set consists only of:

```
cap_chown,cap_dac_override,cap_fowner,cap_fsetid,cap_kill,cap_setgid,cap_setuid,cap_setpcap,cap_net_bind_service,cap_sys_chroot,cap_setfcap=eip
```

we should look at that.
@mbiebl any chance you can test with #19800 if things work for you?

review_comments: Maybe it is better to rename and move this in test-util.[ch]? Then, we can reuse this in the next commit.

hmm, so i thought about this, but i think the checks will end up being highly test specific. i.e. in this PR we already look for CAP_SYS_ADMIN in one place and CAP_NET_RAW in another. And in the seccomp case we could tweak this further if we wanted by also checking NNP.

Hence I figured: let's encode the perms in the individual tests, but not share them between tests, since they shouldn't be opaque but explicit, since different for each, and should be adjusted locally when needed.
OK. That makes sense to me. Thank you fir the consideration.
